text:
Maria G: Heads up — we're seeing a cluster-wide spike of Pending GPU pods in us-west2, started ~10m ago. Many are FailedScheduling: 0/32 nodes are available: 32 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu even though some nodes show free memory.
Trent H: @Maria G can you paste a sample pod describe and node free resources? Might be MIG/shape mismatch or taints.
Maria G: sample from one pending pod:
```
Events:
  Normal  Scheduled  10m   default-scheduler  Successfully assigned ml/train-xyz to node-usw2-07
  Warning FailedScheduling  9m   kubelet  0/32 nodes are available: 32 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
```
Node snapshot (short):
```
node-usw2-07  allocatable: nvidia.com/gpu=1  capacity: nvidia.com/gpu=2  used: 1  free: 1
node-usw2-08  allocatable: nvidia.com/gpu=0  capacity: nvidia.com/gpu=2  used: 2  free: 0
```
Anya P: hmm — allocator shows allocatable 0 on some nodes because MIG partitioning was applied but kubelet hasn't published correct allocatable. Also we recently landed the mixed-MIG node image in that pool.
Samir K: autoscaler-bot reported scale attempts failed due to quota and pool limits. autoscaler-bot: "scale aborted: nodepool-usw2-gpu maxNodes reached (10) and project GPU quota 120 would be exceeded by +4" :no_entry:
Maria G: so cluster has physical capacity, but pods can't land: two likely issues — allocatable mismatch on MIG nodes and nodepool max cap hit preventing scale-out to homogenize packing.
Trent H: also seeing many small single-gpu pods pinned with nodeSelector to nodepool-usw2-gpu. Mixed sizes (1GPU and 4GPU inference) cause binpacking holes when larger pods can't fit into partially used nodes.
Anya P: quick mitigation: 1) cordon problematic mixed-MIG nodes, 2) drain and restart kubelet to refresh allocatable, 3) temporarily relax nodepool maxNodes to allow autoscaler to create fresh homogeneous nodes.
Samir K: steps I can trigger right now:
- uncordon/cordon: `kubectl cordon node-usw2-08`
- drain: `kubectl drain node-usw2-08 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`
- bump nodepool maxNodes to 15 (will need approvals)
infra-oncall: we also need to check IP address exhaustion in that AZ — VPC secondary ip pools are near limit which can prevent new node provisioning.
Maria G: good call. ran `gcloud compute addresses list` and saw /24 subpool at 92% used in us-west2-a. autoscaler can request nodes but provisioning fails silently in cloud provider.
Trent H: so root causes: allocatable inconsistency from MIG mixing + AZ IP exhaustion + nodepool maxNodes cap. That's why pods report Insufficient GPU even with apparent free slices.
Anya P: longer-term we should:
- split nodepools by MIG profile (homogeneous pools) so requests pack more predictably
- enforce admission controller to reject pods that request weird GPU shapes or label them for the right pool
- add an autoscaler preflight that checks cloud quota/IP capacity and surface errors into cluster events
Samir K: temporary runbook I'm applying now: 1) cordon + drain 2) restart kubelet on affected nodes 3) bump nodepool maxNodes to 14 4) open ticket to infra network to expand secondary IP ranges in us-west2-a 5) scale up a new homogenous pool of g5-standard nodes and migrate inference there.
autoscaler-bot: scale action attempted: requested 4 nodes in nodepool-usw2-gpu -> provisioning failed: quota/ip-limit -> aborted
Maria G: applying drain on two worst nodes and will watch pending queue. If we still have holes after restarts, we should temporarily enable binpack-affinity policy (pack small pods together) to reduce fragmentation.
Trent H: can we add a short-term admission webhook to coerce all 1GPU training pods to prefer the new pool via `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`?
Anya P: yes — we can inject nodeAffinity in the mutating webhook for the ml namespace, low risk and can be rolled back.
infra-oncall: I'm creating the network ticket and asking cloud provider to increase secondary IP pool in us-west2-a; ETA 2-4 hours.
Maria G: thanks — will monitor. Current pending count: 62 pods across ml and inference namespaces. If autoscaler can't add nodes in 20m we should engage SRE paging.
Samir K: noted. I'll also file a cost justification for a small dedicated reserve pool (2 nodes) for bursty GPU workloads to avoid repeated scale failures — includes cost estimate ~ $5k/mo but saves 4-6 hours of downtime per month.
Anya P: +1 on reserve pool and on splitting pools. Also adding an eval to our Optimize tool to detect packing inefficiency (wasted GPU cores per node >20% for 3 consecutive hours) to trigger alerts.
Maria G: ok team, executing the runbook now. Will post updates.
Trent H: :eyes:
Maria G: update (10m): drained 2 nodes, kubelet restart fixed allocatable publish on 3 nodes, pending dropped to 18. Waiting for infra-oncall network update to allow new node creation.
infra-oncall: network ticket created: INC-8891, requested extra /24, provider responded: provisioning in progress.
Samir K: overall root cause summary for postmortem: mixed-MIG node image + stale allocatable + AZ IP exhaustion + conservative nodepool caps => binpacking holes and prevented autoscaler recovery. Action items assigned.
Maria G: thanks everyone. I'll start a short postmortem draft in #postmortems once things are stable.
